**Finding submitted: `missing` (TRANSITION), confidence 0.85.**

What I found:
- **Section 13 (p0078)** puts the exit burden entirely on us — *Client* must arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days. It confirms we retain ownership of domains and Client Content, but ownership is not a delivery right.
- **Section 14 (p0079)** only continues services to the end of the month following our termination notice.
- **Section 10 (Confidentiality)** has no return-or-destroy mechanic at all, so there is nothing to repurpose.
- Searches for return/export/transition/delete/migrate turned up no vendor-side obligation anywhere in the document.

Since TrueLink hosts the Web Site and holds our borrower and loan data, this falls short of even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). I inserted a new **Section 14a** immediately after the termination clause (avoiding renumbering of Sections 15–30, which are cross-referenced in the survival provision at p0090) requiring: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter — with a 90-day fallback flagged in the comment. Redline validated `ok:true`.
